description: RAG evaluation benchmark for 6 research papers: ResNet, BERT, Transformer, YOLO, MobileNets, and Pruning Survey. Covers Computer Vision, NLP, and Model Compression domains with factual, conceptual, and cross-paper synthesis questions.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications
Pruning and Quantization for Deep Neural Network Acceleration: A Survey

questions.question: What is the core innovation introduced by the ResNet paper?
questions.evidence_rationale: Paper title and abstract explicitly state 'residual learning framework' to ease training of deeper networks
questions.notes: Tests extraction of paper's main contribution from title and abstract

questions.question: How many layers did the deepest ResNet model achieve on ImageNet?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 7 explicitly states '152-layer ResNet has a single-model top-5 validation error of 4.49%'
questions.notes: Tests precise numerical fact extraction

questions.question: What problem does ResNet solve that prevented training very deep neural networks?
questions.evidence_rationale: Abstract states 'Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of research motivation

questions.question: What does residual function F(x) represent in the ResNet formulation?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 3 states residual block 'has two or three layers (Fig. 5)'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of residual block structure

questions.question: Beyond ImageNet classification, what other vision task did ResNet excel at?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 10 discusses object detection with Faster R-CNN, page 12 mentions winning localization task
questions.notes: Tests knowledge of paper's broader impact beyond classification

questions.question: What does BERT stand for and what is its key innovation?
questions.evidence_rationale: Title and abstract explicitly define BERT acronym and describe bidirectional pre-training
questions.notes: Tests basic identification of paper's contribution

questions.question: What is the masked language model (MLM) objective used in BERT?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 4 explains: 'we simply mask some percentage of the input tokens at random, and then predict those masked tokens'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of BERT's core training method

questions.question: What is BERT's GLUE score and how much improvement did it achieve?
questions.evidence_rationale: Abstract states 'pushing the GLUE score to 80.5% (7.7% point absolute improvement)'
questions.notes: Tests precise metric extraction from abstract

questions.question: Why is BERT's approach better than training separate left-to-right and right-to-left models?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 8 states '(a) this is twice as expensive as a single bidirectional model; (b) this is non-intuitive for tasks like QA'
questions.notes: Tests deep understanding of BERT's design choices

questions.question: What organization developed BERT?
questions.evidence_rationale: Author affiliations on page 1 list 'Google AI Language'
questions.notes: Tests metadata extraction

questions.question: What is the key architectural innovation of the Transformer model?
questions.evidence_rationale: Abstract states model 'based entirely on attention, replacing recurrent layers'
questions.notes: Tests identification of Transformer's main innovation

questions.question: What is scaled dot-product attention and what components does it use?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 4 Figure 2 caption and text describe 'weight assigned to each value is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of attention mechanism components

questions.question: What BLEU score did the Transformer achieve on WMT 2014 English-to-German translation?
questions.evidence_rationale: Abstract states 'new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8'
questions.notes: Tests precise numerical metric extraction

questions.question: Why are convolutional layers more expensive than recurrent layers according to the Transformer paper?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 7 states 'Convolutional layers are generally more expensive than recurrent layers, by a factor of k'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of computational complexity comparisons

questions.question: What makes the Transformer the first sequence transduction model of its kind?
questions.evidence_rationale: Conclusion on page 10 states 'the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing the recurrent layers'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of paper's historical claim

questions.question: What is the main innovation of YOLO compared to prior object detection methods?
questions.evidence_rationale: Abstract describes 'unified' approach and title emphasizes 'You Only Look Once'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of YOLO's key innovation

questions.question: What input resolution change did YOLO make for detection compared to classification pretraining?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 3 states 'we increase the input resolution of the network from 224 × 224 to 448 × 448'
questions.notes: Tests extraction of specific technical details

questions.question: What type of errors does YOLO make more frequently compared to state-of-the-art systems?
questions.evidence_rationale: Abstract states 'YOLO makes more localization errors'
questions.notes: Tests identification of acknowledged limitations

questions.question: How does YOLO handle multiple objects in a single image?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 5 states 'YOLO predicts both bounding boxes and class probabilities for multiple objects of multiple classes in an image'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of YOLO's multi-object capability

questions.question: What performance boost does combining Fast R-CNN with YOLO provide?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 7 states 'Fast R-CNN gets a 2.3% improvement from the combination with YOLO'
questions.notes: Tests extraction of specific performance metrics

questions.question: What is the core building block that makes MobileNets efficient?
questions.evidence_rationale: Abstract mentions 'depthwise separable convolutions' and page 3 explains the mechanism
questions.notes: Tests identification of MobileNets' key innovation

questions.question: What does depthwise convolution do and what is its limitation?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 3 states 'it only filters input channels, it does not combine them to create new features'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of depthwise convolution mechanism and limitations

questions.question: What are the two hyperparameters MobileNets introduces to trade off latency and accuracy?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 5 mentions 'two hyper-parameters: width multiplier and resolution multiplier'
questions.notes: Tests knowledge of MobileNets' configuration parameters

questions.question: What face recognition model did MobileNets adapt for mobile deployment?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 7 discusses adapting 'FaceNet model' for mobile deployment using distillation
questions.notes: Tests knowledge of MobileNets applications

questions.question: What organization developed MobileNets?
questions.evidence_rationale: Author affiliations on page 1 list 'Google Inc.'
questions.notes: Tests metadata extraction

questions.question: What are the two main categories of techniques covered in the pruning survey?
questions.evidence_rationale: Title explicitly states 'Pruning and Quantization'
questions.notes: Tests identification of survey scope

questions.question: What pruning ratio did the survey report achieving on CIFAR-10 while maintaining performance?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 11 mentions 'pruning ratio up to 88.2% on the CIFAR-10 dataset'
questions.notes: Tests extraction of specific quantitative results

questions.question: How can pruning help improve accuracy according to the survey?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 11 states 'By reducing the number of network parameters, pruning techniques can also help to reduce over-fitting'
questions.notes: Tests understanding of pruning benefits beyond compression

questions.question: What bit-width does TensorRT typically use for quantized inference?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 22 discusses TensorRT's 8-bit integer quantization implementation
questions.notes: Tests knowledge of practical quantization implementations

questions.question: What challenges motivate the need for pruning and quantization according to the survey?
questions.evidence_rationale: Page 1 mentions 'require significant computation resources and energy costs' as motivation
questions.notes: Tests understanding of research motivation

questions.question: Compare the depth of the deepest models in ResNet versus experiments mentioned in the Transformer paper.
questions.evidence_rationale: ResNet paper reports 152 layers; Transformer uses attention layers instead of depth in the same sense
questions.notes: Tests ability to compare architectural approaches across papers

questions.question: How do both BERT and the Transformer paper relate to attention mechanisms?
questions.evidence_rationale: BERT uses Transformer architecture bidirectionally; Transformer paper introduces the attention-based architecture
questions.notes: Tests understanding of architectural relationships between papers

questions.question: Which papers address real-time inference as a primary concern?
questions.evidence_rationale: YOLO emphasizes real-time detection, MobileNets targets mobile efficiency, Pruning Survey addresses deployment challenges
questions.notes: Tests identification of common themes across multiple papers

questions.question: How do MobileNets and the Pruning Survey both address model compression?
questions.evidence_rationale: MobileNets uses efficient convolutions; Pruning Survey covers parameter reduction techniques
questions.notes: Tests comparison of different compression approaches

questions.question: Which computer vision papers deal with object-level understanding versus image-level classification?
questions.evidence_rationale: ResNet focuses on image classification; YOLO tackles object detection with localization
questions.notes: Tests understanding of different computer vision tasks

questions.question: What pre-training strategy do BERT and transfer learning approaches in computer vision share?
questions.evidence_rationale: BERT pre-trains then fine-tunes; ResNet uses ImageNet pre-training for detection
questions.notes: Tests understanding of transfer learning across domains

questions.question: How do depthwise separable convolutions in MobileNets relate to the efficiency goals of pruning?
questions.evidence_rationale: Both approaches reduce computation - MobileNets through architectural design, pruning through parameter removal
questions.notes: Tests deep comparison of efficiency strategies

questions.question: Which papers were published in 2015 and what domains do they represent?
questions.evidence_rationale: Both ResNet and YOLO papers are from 2015 and address computer vision
questions.notes: Tests metadata knowledge and temporal relationships

questions.question: What role does Google Research play across the papers in this corpus?
questions.evidence_rationale: Google authored BERT, Transformer, and MobileNets papers
questions.notes: Tests recognition of institutional contributions

questions.question: How do attention mechanisms in Transformers differ from the skip connections in ResNets?
questions.evidence_rationale: Transformers use dynamic attention weighting; ResNets use fixed identity mappings
questions.notes: Tests deep technical comparison across architectures

questions.question: What is Microsoft Research's contribution to deep learning according to the corpus?
questions.evidence_rationale: ResNet paper authors are from Microsoft Research
questions.notes: Tests institutional contribution recognition

questions.question: Which paper addresses the longest sequence lengths and what technique enables this?
questions.evidence_rationale: Transformer paper discusses handling long sequences with O(1) path length via attention
questions.notes: Tests understanding of architectural advantages for sequence modeling

questions.question: What specific quantization bit-width appears in multiple papers' discussions?
questions.evidence_rationale: Survey discusses 8-bit quantization prominently
questions.notes: Tests recognition of common quantization practices

questions.question: Which papers address challenges in training versus inference optimization?
questions.evidence_rationale: ResNet focuses on training deep networks; MobileNets and Pruning focus on efficient inference
questions.notes: Tests understanding of different optimization objectives

questions.question: How do YOLO's localization errors compare to BERT's handling of question answering tasks?
questions.evidence_rationale: Both papers acknowledge task-specific challenges in different modalities
questions.notes: Tests ability to compare limitations across very different domains

questions.question: What year range do the Phase 9B papers span and which is the most recent?
questions.evidence_rationale: ResNet/YOLO from 2015, Pruning Survey from 2021 (arXiv 2101)
questions.notes: Tests temporal awareness of research evolution

questions.question: Which papers contribute to natural language processing and what are their key differences?
questions.evidence_rationale: Transformer introduces architecture; BERT applies it with bidirectional pre-training
questions.notes: Tests understanding of NLP paper relationships

questions.question: How many total pages across all six Phase 9B papers?
questions.evidence_rationale: Metadata shows: ResNet 12, BERT 16, Transformer 15, YOLO 10, MobileNets 9, Pruning Survey 41 = 103 total
questions.notes: Tests ability to aggregate metadata across corpus

questions.question: Which paper is a survey rather than presenting novel methods, and what does it survey?
questions.evidence_rationale: Title explicitly states 'Pruning and Quantization for Deep Neural Network Acceleration: A Survey'
questions.notes: Tests identification of paper types in corpus

questions.question: What architectural paradigm shift do the Transformer and BERT papers represent compared to ResNet and traditional CNNs?
questions.evidence_rationale: Transformer/BERT use attention mechanisms for sequences; ResNet uses convolutional layers for images
questions.notes: Tests high-level understanding of architectural evolution and domain differences
